## 1st Level - Guardian Magic

You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Guardian table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know.

Whenever you gain a sorcerer level, you can replace one spell you gained from this feature with another spell of the same level. The new spell must be an abjuration or a transmutation spell from the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list.

Starting at 1st level, your selfless nature begins to show in your spellcasting. Starting at 6th level, you harness the ability to spread your talents to your allies. Once per turn, as a bonus action, you can strengthen an ally's next spell or attack with a Metamagic option you have access to, spending sorcery points as you would to use the options normally. These options last for a minute. The viable Metamagic options are as listed:

### Quickened Assault

When your target casts a spell that has a casting time of 1 action, they can choose to change the casting time to 1 bonus action for this casting.

Alternatively, they can make one melee or ranged weapon attack as a bonus action.

When the target casts a spell, they can choose to cast it without any somatic or verbal components.

When the target rolls damage for a spell or weapon attack, they can reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). They must use the new rolls.

When the target casts a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw to resist its effects, they can give one target of the spell disadvantage on its first saving throw made against the spell.

## 2nd Level - Blood Channeling

When you choose this arcane tradition at 2nd level, you are able to use your own depleted life essence to channel your magical abilities. Whenever your current hit points are below your hit point maximum, you can use your own body as an arcane focus.

In addition, when casting a wizard spell that requires a costly material component, you can forego the component by taking 1d10 necrotic damage per 50 gp of the cost of the component (minimum 1d10). This damage can’t be reduced in any way. If this damage reduces you to 0 hit points, the spell fails but the spell slot is not expended.

## 2nd Level - Sanguine Burst

Also at 2nd level, you learn how to weave your life force into a spell you cast, boosting its intensity at the cost of your vitality. Whenever you roll damage for a spell you’ve cast of 1st level or higher, you can choose to take necrotic damage equal to the spell’s level to reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum one). This damage can’t be reduced in any way, and you must use the new rolls.

## 6th Level - Bond of Mutual Suffering

At 6th level, when a creature you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to bind your vitality to the attacker and force them to share your pain. The attacker takes damage equal to the damage you took.

This feature cannot be used against constructs or undead. You can use this feature once. You must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

At 14th level, you can use this feature twice between rests.

## 10th Level - Glyph of Hemorrhaging

Starting at 10th level, when you damage a creature with a spell, you can choose to curse that creature for 1 minute. While cursed in this way, whenever the creature is hit by an attack, it takes an extra 1d6 necrotic damage. At the end of each of the creature’s turns, it can make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, ending the curse on a success.

This feature cannot be used against creatures that are undead or constructs. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

## 14th Level - Thicker than Water

Upon reaching 14th level, the blood that flows through your veins is empowered with arcane vigor that mends wounds and helps preserve your life. Whenever a spell or magical effect causes you to regain hit points, you regain an additional number of hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.

In addition, while you are concentrating on a spell, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

You designate a specific condition that triggers the ward, such as a creature crossing a boundary, touching an object, opening a door, or speaking a specific phrase. name: Fey Duelist
description:
The Fey Duelist archetype merges the cunning and agility of a rogue with the enchanting power of the Feywild. These rogues are gifted (or cursed) with the boons of Archfey patrons, weaving magic and mischief into their every movement. They are agile combatants and masters of manipulation, channeling Fey magic to outmaneuver foes, charm allies, and spread chaos on the battlefield.

Whether as emissaries of a Fey court, champions of their Archfey patron, or independent agents who stumbled into the gifts of the Feywild, Fey Duelists tread a fine line between mortal pragmatism and the capricious beauty of the Fey. Their motivations are as varied as the Feywild itself, often driven by a blend of personal ambition, devotion to their patron, or a desire to unweave the chains of mundane reality and reshape the world with Fey-inspired artistry.

#### Playstyle and Motivations

The Fey Duelist excels in roles that combine agility, cunning, and creativity. They bring versatility to combat and social interactions, offering a mix of mobility, control, and spellcasting that allows them to adapt to nearly any situation. Players who enjoy weaving spells and martial combat together will find the Fey Duelist a rewarding choice.

Motivations for a Fey Duelist might include:

*   **Devotion to an Archfey**: Serving a powerful Fey entity as a trusted agent or champion, spreading their influence or carrying out their will.
*   **Personal Freedom**: Using Fey gifts to escape or defy systems of control, embracing the chaotic and whimsical nature of the Feywild.
*   **Vengeance or Redemption**: Seeking to right a past wrong or balance a perceived injustice using the unique powers of the Fey.
*   **Curiosity and Mischief**: Exploring the boundaries of mortal and Fey realms, motivated by wonder and the joy of discovery.

#### Who Would Thrive as a Fey Duelist?

The Fey Duelist appeals to characters who want to:

*   **Command the Social Arena**: Features like *Binding Words* provide robust tools for persuasion, manipulation, and intrigue.
*   **Outmaneuver and Disrupt Enemies**: Abilities like *Elusive Action* and *Distant Dodge* emphasize mobility and tactical positioning.

#### Ideal Players and Characters

*   **The Charismatic Manipulator**: Players who enjoy talking their way out of trouble, influencing NPCs, and using charm to solve problems.
*   **The Tactical Trickster**: Players who like to use cunning, positioning, and the environment to control the flow of combat.
*   **The Fey Enthusiast**: Players who love the whimsical, mysterious, and chaotic themes of the Feywild and want to embody its spirit.

description:
You gain the ability to enter any source of flame and move from inside it to inside another flame within 500 feet. Both flames must be at least the same size as you. You must use 5 feet of movement to enter the source of fire. You instantly know the location of all other flames within 500 feet and, as part of the move used to enter the flame, can either pass into one of those sources of fire or step out of the fire you're in. You appear in a spot of your choice within 5 feet of the destination fire, using another 5 feet of movement. If you have no movement left, you appear within 5 feet of the flame you entered.

You can use this transportation ability once per round for the duration. You must end each turn outside a flame.

You are temporarily immune to fire damage caused by the flame you're stepping into, but not other sources.

name: Form Undead
description:
This spell must be cast within ten minutes after dusk. You must press the idol used for the material component of this spell to the corpse of a creature with a challenge rating of 10 or lower and hold it there for the duration of the casting of this spell. The corpse must be intact for the duration of this spell’s casting— a destroyed corpse causes this spell to fail.

The corpse reanimates, returning to life and using the statblock of the creature it belonged to, with the following changes:

*   its creature type becomes undead
*   its hit point maximum is halved
*   if it has class levels, it loses all of them
*   it loses any legendary actions and legendary resistances
*   It is unable to cast spells
*   it gains immunity to necrotic damage

As a bonus action on each of your turns, you can mentally command any creature you animated with this spell if the creature is within 120 feet of you (if you control multiple creatures, you can command any or all of them at the same time, issuing the same command to each one). You decide what action the creature will take and where it will move during its next turn, or you can issue a general command, such as to guard a particular chamber or corridor. If you issue no commands, the creature only defends itself against hostile creatures. Once given an order, the creature continues to follow it until its task is complete.

An undead raised by this spell is under your control for 24 hours, after which it makes a charisma saving throw. On a failure, you regain control of it for another 24 hours, whereupon it makes the save again. Each time it fails this saving throw, it gains a cumulative +2 bonus to the Charisma save.

On a success, it is hostile to all creatures (including yourself) and is under no compulsion to follow any orders you give it. It has disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws it makes against you (except for the saving throws it makes to break free from your control).

name: Gnarly Druid
description:
When you take this prestige class, choose two more skills from the Druid skill proficiencies. You are proficient in both of those skills.

## Ascendant Spellcasting

Additionally when you take this prestige class, you gain a new set of spell slots to fuel your spells. You gain spell slots as per the Druid table based on your prestige level minus 20. When you prepare spells for the day, you may now prepare a number of spells equal to your prestige level + your Wisdom modifier.

You learn one Druid cantrip of your choice, and one additional Druid cantrip at 24th and 30th level.

## Transcendent Wild Shape

*21st level.* Your connection to the primal has outgrown mortal limits. You gain one additional use of Wild Shape.

Your known forms increase by 2, and the maximum Challenge Rating for your forms increases by 1 (added to whatever maximum you already have from your class and subclass features). In addition, you may now learn Elemental stat blocks (in place of Beasts) up to CR 1 as known forms, representing your growing kinship with the raw substance of the world.

## Expanded Druid Circle

*22nd level.* Your practice of the old ways deepens and broadens. You may choose the same Druid Circle you already belong to, or you may choose a new one to reflect the different truths nature has revealed to you.

Your choice grants you additional features at 22nd level, and again at 26th and 34th level.

## Primal Resilience

*23rd level.* Nature itself shields you from harm. You gain resistance to poison damage and immunity to the Poisoned condition. While you are Wild Shaped, you also have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.

## Ability Score Improvement

*24th, 28th, 32nd, 36th, and 39th level.* You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two of your ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. You may select a feat instead of an Ability Score Improvement.

## Greater Beast Spells

*25th level.* Your magic no longer cares what shape you wear. While using Wild Shape, you can cast any Druid spell you have prepared, including spells with a Material component that has a cost or is consumed, provided you have access to the required component or a Druidic Focus that can be worn or held in your current form (at your DM's discretion for unusual anatomies).

## Elemental Ascendancy

*27th level.* Your command of the elements grows so complete that you no longer have to choose a single expression of it. You now have both options granted by Elemental Fury and Improved Elemental Fury, improved as follows.

***Potent Spellcasting.*** Once on each of your turns when you deal damage with a Druid spell of 1st level or higher, you can add your Wisdom modifier to that damage.

***Primal Strike.*** The extra damage of your Primal Strike increases to 3d8.

## Master of Beasts

*29th level.* Your mastery of shapechanging reaches new heights. Your known forms increase by 2, and the maximum Challenge Rating for your forms increases by 2 (added to whatever maximum you already have from your class, subclass, and other features). Forms you adopt may now be Huge.

## Apex Form

*30th level.* You can, as a Bonus Action, expend two uses of Wild Shape to instead take the form of a Primal Avatar: a towering, elemental-infused shape of your own design (DM's discretion on appearance) using the stat block of any Beast, Elemental, or Monstrosity with a Challenge Rating up to your Proficiency Bonus + 4 (CR 10 for most characters). While in this form, you retain the benefits of Greater Beast Spells and Elemental Ascendancy, and you gain temporary hit points equal to five times your prestige level. This form lasts for up to 10 minutes, until you drop to 0 hit points, or until you revert to your normal form as a Bonus Action.

description:
The Memory Thief is a sorcerer touched by the silent weight of unspoken thoughts, lost truths, and stolen moments. Whether chosen by a god of shadows and secrets or born with the uncanny ability to pierce the veil of another’s mind, these sorcerers draw power not from raw elements—but from **memory, emotion, and identity** itself.

Every spell is an intrusion, every glance a chance to unravel another’s story. They are masters of **mental trespass and psychic influence**, collecting knowledge the way others collect coins. Some act as spies for hidden powers like *Vhaeraun*, gods of forbidden knowledge, or remnants of psionic empires. Others awaken to their abilities after surviving moments of profound trauma or divine contact—left able to **steal what others cannot even remember**.

*"Thoughts and Emotions are the truest form of currency. I never pay full price." - Memory Thief*

### *Playstyle and Motivations*

*The Memory Thief excels at **subtle control**, **emotional manipulation**, and **deep utility** in both narrative and combat play. With features that allow you to read and manipulate the thoughts and motivations of others, this subclass rewards **strategic roleplay**, **creative problem-solving**, and players who love to know more than they should.*

*   ***Reclaim the Past**: Seeking to recover a stolen or fragmented identity by stitching together memories from others.*
*   ***Weaponize Secrets**: Collecting powerful memories from kings, archmages, or ancient evils to manipulate the tides of history or blackmail enemies into silence.*
*   ***Protect the Mindscape**: Standing as a psychic guardian or counter-spy, exposing hidden corruption or breaking mind control through counter-manipulation.*

* * *

*The Memory Thief is perfect for players who want to:*

*   ***Influence Story Through Subtlety**: Gain leverage by collecting key memories, discovering hidden motives, or creating complex emotional bonds with NPCs.*
*   ***Play with Identity and Perception**: Use your magic to assume false roles, mimic memories, or veil your soul against detection.*
*   ***Master Battlefield Presence Without Direct Violence**: Weaken enemies emotionally, disrupt their thoughts, and track them across time and space.*

* * *

***Ideal Players and Characters***

*🧠 **The Intrigue Manipulator***

*Players who thrive in espionage-heavy or social-intrigue campaigns, especially those who enjoy steering conversations with secrets and subtle leverage.*

*🕯 **The Shadowed Seer***

*Players who love mysteries and clues, piecing together narrative threads from the minds of others, treating every memory like a breadcrumb on a hidden trail.*

*Players who want to play with masks, personas, and the line between truth and falsehood—taking on aspects of others through their memories, voices, and fears.*

# Class Features

## PL 21: Proficiencies

When you take this prestige class, choose two additional skills from the Warlock skill list. You gain proficiency in both.

## PL 21: Ascended Pact Magic

Your amount of available pact slots increases per the Morelock Table.

## PL 22: Improved Magical Cunning

You can now Expend an action, bonus action and all your movement to use Magical cunning.

## PL 23: Patron

Your eldritch mastery has grown so strong you can now have 2 different patrons without conflict, You may choose the same warlock patron, or you may choose a new one. At PL 23, PL 26, PL 31 and PL37, you gain more features from your warlock patron.

## PL 24: Ability Score Improvement

At PL 24, 28, 32, 36, and 39, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or two ability scores by 1. As normal, you cannot increase a score above 20 (unless another feature allows it). You may select a Feat instead of an ASI.

## PL 25: Journeyman Pact Magic

Your Pact Slots increase in power. All of your available Warlock Pact Slots are now 6th level. You do not learn any new 6th-level spells to cast with these slots; they can only be used to upcast the Warlock spells you know of 5th level or lower, or to cast the specific 6th-level Warlock spells you have already learned through your Mystic Arcanum feature.

## PL 29: Ascendant Contact Patron

Your connection to your patron transcends the boundaries of the planes. When you use your Warlock Contact Patron feature to cast *Contact Other Plane*, the casting time is reduced to 1 Action, and you do not need to speak aloud to ask your questions.

Additionally, once per Long Rest, you can cast the *Gate* spell without expending a Pact Slot or requiring material components. When cast in this way, the portal can only open to the home domain of your Patron, allowing you to step into their realm.

## PL31: Heightened Mystic Arcunam

Choose another level 6 Warlock spell as this arcanum.

You can cast your 6th level arcanum spell twice without expending a spell slot, and you must finish a Long Rest before you can cast it in this way again.

As shown in the Morelock Features table, you gain another Warlock spell of your choice that can be cast in this way when you reach Warlock levels 33 (level 7 spell), 35 (level 8 spell), and 37 (level 9 spell), these can be cast as arcanums twice per long rest. You regain all uses of your Mystic Arcanum when you finish a Long Rest.

name: Night Reaver
description:
*You learn the art of siphoning life from dying enemies and combining it with negetive energy to imbue necromancy into your fighting style. Reavers often kill those who are closest to death, whose spiritual binds are thin enough to cut free and use.* Features:

*   [3rd Level - Criticality](#3rd-level---criticality)
*   [9th Level - Rend](#9th-level---rend)
*   [13th Level - Ward of Mortality](#13th-level---ward-of-mortality)
*   [17th Level - Echo of Reaping](#17th-level---echo-of-reaping)

## 3rd Level - Criticality

Starting at 3rd level, creatures with less than half of their total hit points gain a Death Mark, granting you the following benefits:

*   You gain an additional way to use your sneak attack; you don’t need advantage on the attack roll to use your Sneak Attack against a marked creature, so long as you don’t have disadvantage on the attack roll.
*   Attack rolls against marked creatures crit on 19-20.
*   You have a bonus on attack rolls against marked creatures. This bonus equals half your proficiency bonus.

## 9th Level - Rend

Starting at 9th level, you gain the ability to **rend** those close to death.

When you hit a marked creature with your Sneak Attack, you can deal additional damage equal to your rogue level. Once you use this ability, you may not do so against until you complete a short or long rest. If you reduce a creature to zero hit points with this ability, you regain a use.

## 13th Level - Ward of Mortality

Starting at 13th level, you learn to collect and conserve the life force you steal from dying opponents, which materializes as a ward.

When you hit a marked creature with **rend**, roll your total sneak attack die. You gain temporary hit points equal to the total, unless you already have more.

## 17th Level - Echo of Reaping

Starting at 17th level, you learn to travel to and harness remnants of death.

When you hit a creature with **rend**, you may teleport to a corpse within 90 ft of you as a bonus action, and the next attack you make before the end of your next treats the target as being blood marked. In addition, through a one-minute ritual, you may travel to an area of mass death or a sight where you slew a creature within 2 miles, bringing a number of willing creatures equal to the number of creatures you have killed today (maximum of 10). Once you use this ability, you may not do so again until you complete a long rest.

name: Phantom Ship Charm
description:
This small rusted anchor charm is bound to a cursed, lost ship: The Specter’s Breath. This ship and its crew were lost to the Ethereal Plane centuries ago, cursed to remain there and wander aimlessly until called back by an ancient relic charm. This small charm acts as the ship's tether to the Material Plane.

As an action, you can call out to the ship while holding the charm aloft. If you're within 30 feet of a body of water on the Material Plane, a full-sized anchor appears on the ground in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the water. A wispy, gray chain appears on the anchor that extends into nothingness. After 1 minute, the Specter’s Breath emerges from the Ethereal Plane, pulled by the anchor's chain, and coming to rest in the water nearby. The ship is a longship 70 feet long and 20 feet wide. It's piloted by thirty-four crewmembers and five officers, all of whom are long-dead, ghostly remains of their former selves. They are formless and harmless, but are nevertheless visible and friendly to you and your companions. They can interact with the rigging, sails, and other equipment on the ship, but nothing else while they remain on the Material Plane. While the ship remains, it moves at a speed of 10 miles per hour, or half as much when there isn't any wind. Only you can command it and its crew while the charm is on your person.

The ship may be commanded for up to 10 days, after which you cannot summon it again until a further 10 days have passed.  Every day at dawn the ship and its crew begin to gradually fade over 10 minutes before they are returned to the Ethereal Plane. They may be resummoned the following dusk. The ship returns early if you speak the command phrase "Until the night calls once more," or if the ship takes enough damage that it would be destroyed. Anything not summoned with the ship is dropped into the water below the ship when it disappears.

description:
You attempt to forcefully tear the spirit of a creature from its body, leaving it momentarily defenseless. Choose one humanoid creature within range (creatures under the effects of a spell, feature or magic item that wards them against Undead or possession cannot have their spirit ejected by this spell). The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, their spirit is ejected from their body and manifests as a spectral form within 10 feet of them. The target’s body becomes incapacitated, and has disadvantage on saving throws against effects that would possess them. The spirit resembles their mortal form in almost every way, replicating game statistics but not their possessions. Any damage or other effects that apply to your spirit or physical body affects the other. In addition, the spirit is incorporeal, resistant to all damage except psychic or radiant, and it must choose whether it gets a move, an action, or a bonus action on a turn; it gets only one of the three. The spirit is tethered to the body and cannot move more than 60 feet away from it.

At the start of each of the target’s turns, they can attempt a Wisdom saving throw to end the effect early. If they succeed, their spirit returns to their body, and they regain control at the start of their next turn.

If the body is reduced to 0 hit points while the spirit is still ejected, the creature dies instantly. If killed in this way, its spirit detaches from its corpse as a Specter under your control, the statistics of which are in the Monster Manual.

You can mentally command the Specter or any creature you made with this spell if the creature is within 60 feet of you (if you control multiple creatures, you can command any or all of them at the same time, issuing the same command to each one), and in combat the Specter shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours.

The Specter remains in your service for up to 10 days, at which point it vanishes to the afterlife. While the Specter is in your service, its soul is trapped and cannot be revived. A Remove Curse, Dispel Evil and Good, or Wish spell ends this spells effect.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th or 7th level or higher, the target has disadvantage on its initial saving throw. At 8th or 9th level, the target instead rises as a Poltergeist if killed.

## Firearm Proficiency

At 3rd Level, you have learned to harness the potency of firearms to complement the powers of the storms you chase. You gain proficiency with firearms.

## Thundercrack

Starting at 3rd level, when you take this archetype at 3rd level, you are able to unleash a deafening boom when you use your ranged weapons. Once on each of your turns, when you attack with a ranged weapon, you can force each creature within 10 feet of you to make a constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes 1d8 thunder damage. The damage increases to 2d8 at 11th level.

## Charged Shell

At 7th level, when you take the attack action, you can forgo your extra attack feature to make a single ranged weapon attack. This attack deals triple the damage dice of the weapon you used, and deals lightning damage instead of bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing. This attack is also critical on a d20 roll of 19 or 20 if used during a storm.

## Storm Caller

At 11th level, you have learned to bring storms to you. As an action, you call forth a vortex at a point you can see within 60 feet. The vortex is a cylinder with a radius of 30 feet, and a height of 90 feet. The vortex counts as a storm for the purposes of Charged Shell.

As a bonus action on each of your turns while the vortex lasts, you can target a creature inside, striking them with a bolt of lightning. The target must make a dexterity saving throw, taking 3d10 lightning on a failure, or half as much on a successful save.

The vortex lasts for 10 minutes, and once used, cannot be summoned again until you finish a long rest, or spend a spell slot of at least 3rd level or higher to summon it again. No more than 1 vortex can exist at once.

## Eye of the Storm

At 15th level, you gain resistance to lightning and thunder damage.

Additionally, you can target yourself with the bolt of lightning from your storm caller ability. If you do so, instead of taking damage, your next charged shell attack deals extra damage equal to twice the amount of damage the lightning would have dealt. This also causes the attack to be critical on a d20 roll of 18, 19, or 20.

This large sniper rifle is made with thicker material to propel projectiles at very long distances without losing accuracy, delivering destructive capabilities that can even pierce metal gates. Each shot made with this rifle sends a loud ripple on the battlefield that would bring dread whether or not they will be the next target. With a flick of your wrist, you magically start the process of completing a small and simple task, such as flipping a book page, buttering bread, or heating a cup of tea, without any physical interaction. ## Planar Tether

When you form this pact at 1st level, you are granted the ability to tether your summoned creatures to your plane, granting them additional strengths.

When you cast a warlock spell that summons a single creature, you may undergo a special ritual during the casting of the spell. Doing so changes the spell's casting time to 10 minutes, and the summon lasts until it is dispelled. If the spell normally requires concentration, you may ignore the requirement.

When you summon a creature in this way, it is referred to as your tether, and it gains the following benefits:

*   You can replace its hit points with 5 x your warlock level.
*   It adds your proficiency bonus to its damage rolls.
*   If the creatures to-hit bonus is less than that of your spell attack bonus, it may instead use your spell attack bonus when attacking.

You learn the Find Familiar spell, it counts as a warlock spell for you, and it does not count towards your total spells known.

If you summon another creature using this ritual, any previous creatures summoned by it are immediately dispelled. After you complete this ritual, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

## Ethereal Stores

Starting at 6th level, you can briefly store items away for later use. You can cast the \[Wristpocket\] spell a number of times equal to your charisma modifier without expending a spell slot. When you do, the stored object is sent to the ethereal plane, and the spell does not require concentration. You regain all expended uses of this ability when you finish a long rest.

Additionally, you can see into the ethereal plane up to 10 ft.

## Undying Binds

At 10th level, when tether drops to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to expend a pact slot. Doing so will restore 50 hit points to the summon.

## Sacrificial Summoning

Starting on 14th level, while your Planar Tether summon is active, you can use an action to sacrifice part of yourself to empower it and your spells, doing so allows you to channel this ability until your next long rest, or until you end it as an action. While channeling this ability, you have the following effects:

*   Your hit point maximum is reduced by 30.
*   You have disadvantage on Constitution checks and saving throws, except for those made to maintain concentration.
*   Your tether has advantage on all saving throws
*   You can use a bonus action to give your tether temporary hit points equal to your warlock level
*   Creatures within 10 ft of your tether have disadvantage on saving throws against your spells.

If you end this ability early, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.

## Design Notes

This is intended to be a thematic and lore-accurate depiction of abilities, influences and blessings described in canon materials as being granted to various faiths, groups or members of organizations affiliated with The Masked Lord (in this case Vhaeraun-inspired)

### Playstyle and Motivations

The Masked Lord excels at adaptability, infiltration, opportunistic combat, and deceptive utility. Its three Masks allow the warlock to shift between thief, warrior, and mage, while later features turn shadow, enemy attacks, and hostile magic into tools of their own.

*   **Wear the Right Mask**: Adapt your skills and tactics to the task at hand through the Masks of the Thief, Warrior, and Mage.
*   **Become the Perfect Instrument**: Approach problems as an operative rather than a specialist—using stealth, weapons, magic, or cunning as circumstances demand.
*   **Turn Strength Against Its Owner**: Redirect hostile attacks, steal enemy spells, and exploit aggression rather than meeting force with force.
*   **Shape the Shadows**: Create useful equipment from shadowstuff and treat darkness as a tangible resource rather than simple concealment.
*   **Act Through Subtlety**: Favor infiltration, positioning, preparation, deception, and precise intervention over overt displays of power.
*   **Become the Unseen Hand**: Progress toward influencing the Material Plane from beyond its boundaries, acting where enemies struggle to reach you.

### Who Would Thrive as a Masked Lord Warlock?

The subclass is ideal for players who want to:

*   **Shift Roles Easily**: Move between infiltrator, combatant, investigator, and spellcaster depending on the mission.
*   **Reward Creative Problem-Solving**: Use mundane tools, shadowcraft, positioning, and unusual applications of magic to overcome obstacles.
*   **Play an Arcane Operative**: Blend rogue-like utility, martial capability, and warlock magic into the feel of a supernatural agent.
*   **Exploit Opportunities**: React to enemy actions and changing battlefield conditions rather than relying on a single repeated tactic.
*   **Counter Enemy Magic**: Capture and reuse hostile spells through Darkspell Mantle.
*   **Remain Difficult to Predict**: Change your capabilities and approach so enemies cannot easily define your role or anticipate your methods.

### Ideal Players and Characters

*   🎭 **The Master of Masks** — Enjoys changing tactics, identities, and roles to meet different challenges.
*   🗡️ **The Shadow Operative** — Favors infiltration, espionage, sabotage, and practical problem-solving.
*   ♟️ **The Tactical Opportunist** — Watches the battlefield carefully and turns enemy actions into openings.
*   🕶️ **The Arcane Counterspy** — Enjoys stealing, redirecting, and exploiting hostile magic.
*   🌑 **The Shadow Adept** — Wants shadow to evolve from concealment into substance, tool, and eventually a means of transcending the Material Plane.
*   🦊 **The Cunning Generalist** — Values versatility over specialization and wants a useful answer to many different kinds of challenges.

**Core Philosophy**: Never be limited to what others believe you are. Change the mask, change the method, and make every strength your enemy reveals another tool in your hand.

name: Thought Forms
description:
Through carefully crafted thought projections and the transmutation of mental energies, you create a field of potentiality around you, exceeding your normal limitations. When you cast this spell you create 6 Thought Forms. You can consume these Thought Forms in a number of ways, granting additional benefits depending on your choice:

*   When you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you misses with an attack, you can consume any number of Thought Form. They gain a +2 bonus to the attack roll equal to the number of Thought Forms consumed, potentially turning the miss into a hit.
*   Once per turn, when you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you take the Attack action, you can consume 2 Thought Forms to allow them to make an additional attack as part of that same action.
*   When you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you take damage from an attack, you can consume any number of Thought Forms as a reaction, granting them 10 temporary hit points for each Thought Form consumed. These temporary hit points last until the start of your next turn.
*   When you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw against a spell or magical effect, you can use your reaction to consume any number of your Thought Forms. They gain a +2 bonus to your saving throw for each Thought Form consumed, potentially turning the failure into a success.

description:
You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this magic weapon. Tidepiercer is a spellcasting focus for you.

**Sapphire Ferocity**

You can add your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1) to the damage rolls of attacks you make with this weapon. This bonus is in addition to the normal ability modifier you add to the damage roll. It applies to each attack you make with Tidepiercer (including opportunity attacks), but not to damage dealt by spells.

While attuned, you always know the direction and distance to the nearest coastline. Once per dawn, spend 10 minutes using Tidepiercer to cast augury without material components; the omen appears as foam-light along the blade.

**Sapphire Refrain**

You can weave brief, tide-kissed refrains into your inspiration. A number of times per short or long rest equal to your proficiency bonus, when a creature you can see rolls your Bardic Inspiration die or when you expend a die with Unsettling Words, you can invoke one of the following effects (no action):

*   **Clear the Wake.** The inspired creature may end the charmed or frightened condition on itself.
*   **Undercurrent (Unsettling Words only).** If the trigger was your Unsettling Words, you may instead choose the target of Unsettling Words. That creature can’t make opportunity attacks until the start of your next turn.

description:
You magically expand the dimensions of an existing container, room, or otherwise fully enclosed space beyond its physical limits. Select an existing physical space (no larger than 125 sq ft.) with at most one single point of entry such as a lid, door, window or flap, (no larger than 10 sq ft), and with a solid border (no transparent walls, windows, etc.). As a part of this spell, the caster must inscribe runes around the opening and the borders of the space to maintain its external structure. The interior dimensions of that space expand by up to 5 feet in any direction that you choose as the spell takes effect, warping to accommodate any items or creatures inside.

When the spell ends, the space returns to its normal size and any items or occupants unable to fit in the original space are softly ejected through the opening. If there is no opening or the objects cannot fit through it, the items or creatures are scattered randomly in the Astral Plane as determined by the GM.

Casting this spell in the same space every day for 30 days makes the effect permanent; further castings can be used to expand an existing Transdimensional Space beyond its size provided that it still has a single exterior border with no more than one point of entry.
